title: LIN-4292 tidy-after: one spelling for DOM element access across public/, with a check (the edges its blind reads named)
description:
## Goal

`public/` uses one spelling for DOM element access: an element is trusted to have its methods. A check keeps the old spelling from coming back. Where a node really might not be an Element, the code says so on that line.

## Context

LIN-4292 (`b389f9b02`) removed the method-presence guards (`x.querySelector ? … : null`, `x.matches && …`, `x.closest ? …`, `x.getAttribute ? …`) from four files: `prompt-section.js`, `common.js`, `dispatch.js` and `task-page.js`. Two blind, code-only reads scored it **better** and **mixed**. Both gave the same reason: the line was drawn by file and method name, not by idiom.

Checked by hand at `b389f9b0`:

* **The same idiom remains in ten files.** It is a guard on `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `matches`, `closest`, `getAttribute` or `contains`, written as `?`, `&&` or `!x.method`. About 17 sites: `ship-journey.js` ×3, `decision-panel.js` ×3, `task-page.js` ×2, `prompt-section.js` ×2, `flight-companion.js` ×2, and one each in `task-chat.js`, `ship-biscuit.js`, `settings-models.js`, `session.js` and `close-out.js`.
* **Two of them sit inside functions LIN-4292 edited,** so those functions now mix both spellings: `slot.contains &&` (`prompt-section.js:1210`, in `paintRun`) and `!drawer.querySelectorAll` (`:1871`, in `keepFocusInDrawer`).
* **Some are legitimate.** `flight-companion.js:950` walks `parentNode` up from an event target, so it can reach non-Element nodes, and `li.getAttribute &&` is a real type check there. An `e.target` can be a Text node.
* **Nothing stops the idiom coming back.** The safety the guards once gave a hand-written test stub now lives in the shared fake DOM and its census.

This is the loop's "after" step. The copies a blind read names at a change's edges become a small tidy-after in the same area.

## This step

* **Remove every remaining guard** where the object is an Element by construction. Keep every object null check the expression had, so each line returns the same value on a real DOM.
* **Where a node may not be an Element** (a walk up `parentNode`, an `e.target`), keep the check and mark the line with a short inline reason that the check recognises. The reason lives beside the code, not in a list.
* **A check** (a unit test beside the other source-shape checks, in the style of `test-server-listen-bind.test.js`) that fails a method-presence guard on these methods in `public/*.js` unless the line carries the marker. Its fixtures pin both cases.

**Not this ticket:** merging `readDispatchExecControls` and `readDispatchPresetPicker` (a blind read noted them as a near-identical pair); any behaviour change.

## Done when

* The check passes, and fails on a seeded guard in a fixture.
* Every remaining guard carries its marker and reason.
* The unit suite and E2E pass, with names and counts unchanged.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 20:20, at `b389f9b02`) corrected the description. Here is the person's scope call, in order:

1. **The check first, and its hit list is the work list,** not the hand count above.
   * Make it an AST scan with acorn, as `fake-dom-census.test.js` does. Don't copy `stripComments` a thirteenth time. The scan matches "a member is tested, then the same member is called on the same receiver".
   * **It covers four spellings:** `x.m ? x.m(…) : …`, `x.m && x.m(…)`, `!x.m` before a call, and `typeof x.m === 'function'` / `!== 'function'`. It covers these methods: `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `matches`, `closest`, `getAttribute` and `contains`.
   * **Fixtures pin:** each spelling; a multi-line guard; `window.matchMedia(…).matches`, which is a `MediaQueryList` property and **not** a guard (the "then called" rule passes it); and an allow-listed entry.
   * Run the scan at the base, and put its list in the PR.
2. **Sort each hit into remove, keep or not-a-guard.** The rule is decided once, here:
   * **Delegated** `e.target` **on click, input, change, focusin or focusout is trusted,** because the browser retargets those events to Elements. Remove those guards. **The description's "an** `e.target` **can be a Text node" was wrong.**
   * A `parentNode` walk that can reach non-Elements is kept. Check `flight-companion.js:950` on the evidence: it stops at `modelListEl`, so it may be removable.
   * A `contains` guard never tests for an Element, because `contains` is on `Node`. Remove it.
   * **The** `close-out.js typeof` **checks (**`:159/161/175`**) are a unit seam:** `close-out-client.test.js` passes a doc without `querySelectorAll`. They stay for now and the check sees them. LIN-4254 moves that suite, and its scope will say to remove them then.
   * Run each file's owning unit suite after each file, because several census suites fire handlers with hand-built `target:` objects.
3. **Exceptions follow the house convention:** an allow-list inside the test, one reason per entry, as in `no-page-wide-label-listener.test.js`. **No inline marker** (that would be a second exception convention), and so no `CLAUDE.md` change. Write each reason in the present tense, saying what is true of that line now.
4. **Not this ticket:**
   * the `typeof el.focus` guards (`prompt-section.js:1053/1219/1856`), the same idiom on a method not listed here, which goes to the notebook;
   * one shared scanner for the source-shape checks;
   * merging `readDispatchExecControls` and `readDispatchPresetPicker`.

"Names and counts unchanged" means: apart from the new test file.

## At merge

* The scan's hit list at the base, and each hit's verdict, are in the PR.
* The check passes, and fails on a seeded guard of each spelling.
* The allow-list is short, and each entry has a true reason.
* The unit suite and E2E pass.

## Implementation Plan

*Implemented as approved in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2320](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2320>) (squash-merged as* `f742e5ac`*, deployed to production). The one deviation from the plan:* `close-out.js main && typeof main.getAttribute` *was kept and allow-listed (not removed) per the ticket's scope call, with a reason reworded in review (commit* `3b71bf96`*); LIN-4312 removes it. The full plan, the Surveys and the pre-prune description are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.*

fits one session. plan-review due: no

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4304 @ b389f9b02

origin/main is LIN-4292's own merge (#2315). The hard part isn't deleting ~17 guards: **the idiom isn't one idiom**, and the ticket's two buckets ("Element by construction" / "might not be an Element") miss three kinds of site.

**1. Not every guard is a method-presence guard.** `.matches` is also a **boolean property of `MediaQueryList`**. `settings-models.js:61` `phone.matches ? form.querySelector(…) : null` is counted in the ticket's ten files, but `phone` is `window.matchMedia(…)`. Removing it changes phone-width behaviour. The same spelling appears at `common.js:3005`, `live-console.js:50`, `ship-journey.js:313` and `flight-companion.js:2012`. A check keyed on the method name plus `?`/`&&` will flag these, and can't honestly carry the marker. The check needs either an exclusion (the receiver came from `matchMedia`) or to drop `matches` in the `x.matches ?` form.

**2. The ticket's count leaves out a third spelling: `typeof x.m === 'function'` / `!== 'function'`.** These are at `close-out.js:159/161/175`, `question-cards.js:468`, `prompt-section.js:881` and `common.js:2356`. Ignore them and the idiom returns under a new spelling; include them and scope grows.

**3. Some guards are unit seams, not type checks.** The ticket says stub safety "now lives in the shared fake DOM and its census". At this commit the census still lists **25** hand-written fake-DOM suites. `close-out.js:168-172` documents "one without `querySelectorAll` (unit seams) reports false". `close-out-client.test.js:150` loads the module with a `document` that has no `querySelector`, and `:245-247` call `pageAlreadyDone` with hand-built docs. Removing those guards throws there unless the stubs change. Several other census suites (`lin-3254-session-run-toggles`, `flight-companion-client`, `common-*-filter-nav`) fire handlers with hand-built `target:` objects. Run each owning suite per removal.

**4. `e.target` is the judgment call.** About eight sites guard `e.target.closest` (`decision-panel` ×3, `ship-journey:640/659`, `session:324`, `ship-biscuit:166`, `task-chat:446`). In a modern browser, the target of click/input/change/focusin is an Element, not a Text node. The only non-Element targets are `document`/`window` from a synthetic dispatch, and I found none in `public/`. The ticket's "an `e.target` can be a Text node" would mark all eight and remove almost nothing. Decide the rule once: `parentNode` walks (`flight-companion.js:950`) get the marker, delegated `e.target` gets trusted. Otherwise the marker becomes the new default.

**Smaller traps.** `contains` is on `Node`, so a `contains` guard never tests "is an Element" (`slot.contains`, `prompt-section.js:1210`, is plain removable). The marker is a comment, and the model test strips comments before matching, so the check has to read the marker from the raw line. The census file notes that importing `stripComments` from `test-server-listen-bind.test.js` re-runs that file's tests, so copy it or use acorn with `onComment`.

**What I'd do first.** Before touching `public/`, write the check with fixtures for: `?`, `&&`, `!x.m`, `typeof`, a MediaQueryList `.matches`, a marked `parentNode` walk, and a multi-line guard. Run it against b389f9b02 and use its list, not the hand count, as the work list. Then sort each hit into remove / mark / not-a-guard. Run the owning unit suite after each file.

## Survey global: LIN-4304 @ b389f9b02

**Where it lands.** Ten client scripts in `public/`, plus one new check next to the ~60 source-shape tests in `tests/unit/`. This area is improving: the fake-DOM census has gone from 56 hand-written fakes to 25, and LIN-4292 started on the idiom. The remaining fakes for `close-out`, `decision-panel`, `session`, `task-chat` and `flight-companion` all define `closest`/`getAttribute`, so the removals should be test-neutral.

**What the obvious way would do**

- **False positives.** `settings-models.js:61` (`phone.matches ?`) and `live-console.js:1648` read `MediaQueryList.matches`, which is a property and not a method. A regex built from the ticket's list would flag them, and they would get a wrong "not an Element" marker. Only flag a member when the same receiver then calls it, and pin `matchMedia` as allowed in a fixture.
- **A spelling the check doesn't cover.** The same guard is also written `typeof x.m === 'function'` (`close-out.js:159/161/175`, `question-cards.js:468`, `prompt-section.js:881`, `common.js:2356`). If the check skips that form, `typeof` becomes the accepted spelling. `close-out.js:159/175` are an injected-doc test seam (`close-out-client.test.js:244-247`), so they stay, but the check should still see them.
- **The marker could end up on most sites.** If "`e.target` may not be an Element" is taken literally, about 9 of the ~16 sites get marked. But these listeners are `click`, `input`, `change` and `focusout`, and the browser retargets all of those to Elements. `flight-companion.js:950` also stops climbing at `modelListEl`. Decide by event type and walk boundary. Honestly, the marker may land on zero or one line.
- **A second exception convention.** `public/` has no inline marker yet. `no-page-wide-label-listener.test.js` scans the same files and keeps its exceptions in an allow-list inside the test. An inline marker is fine, but name it in `CLAUDE.md` next to the fake-DOM line.
- **A thirteenth `stripComments`.** About 12 test files each have their own copy. `fake-dom-census` uses acorn and avoids importing one, because the import re-runs that file's tests. An AST scan ("member tested, then the same member called") is more precise than a line regex.
- **Nothing else needs updating.** No registry lists these sites. The new test adds names, so say in the PR that "names and counts unchanged" means apart from the new file.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:** an AST check covering all four spellings, with `matchMedia` allowed and a fixture for each. Remove nearly every guard. Add one `CLAUDE.md` line.

**Better still, not this task's:** move `pageAlreadyDone`/`boxContext` onto the shared fake so the `typeof` seams can go. Drain the other 25 fakes. Give the source-shape checks one shared scanner. Deal with the `typeof el.focus` guards (`prompt-section.js:1053/1219/1856`), the same idiom on a method the ticket doesn't list.

## LIN-4304 — implemented, PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2320 (branch `feat/lin-4304-one-dom-element-spelling`, commit `8cc40286`)

- **Change:** the 23 method-presence guards on `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `matches`, `closest`, `getAttribute` and `contains` in `public/*.js` are removed where the receiver is an Element by construction. Each removal keeps the null check the expression had. Three `close-out.js` `typeof` seams stay, allow-listed.
- **Check:** `tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js` — acorn AST scan over `public/*.js`, fixtures for all four spellings, allow-list with one reason per entry. Witnessed: fails on the unedited base (23 hits); mutants that blind the `typeof` or early-return rule fail the matching fixtures.
- **Verification:** unit suite 23,828 pass / 0 fail (base 23,811; +17 are the new file, test names otherwise unchanged). E2E 2,004 passed / 1 skipped (pre-existing). CI: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `CI success` all SUCCESS.
- **Follow-up:** none for `lib/`, `routes/` or `server.js` (no matches for the same spellings).

## Review — LIN-4304

PR #2320, head `8cc4028608bbb66d5a9eb14c5f6983da37ea56cf`, on base `b581ac92` (main). One commit, 11 `public/*.js` files and 1 new test. The PR matches the plan's places. Nothing under `public/` or `tests/` changed on main after the ticket was created, apart from the base commit `b581ac92`.

CI: green on head `8cc40286`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `CI success` all passed.

**What I checked myself**
- **Base scan.** I ran the new check against `public/` at base. It fails, and its hits match the PR's table: close-out ×4 (`:62` plus the three `typeof` seams), common `:2356`, decision-panel ×3, flight-companion `:803` and `:950`, prompt-section `:881`, `:1210` and `:1872`, question-cards `:468`, session, ship-biscuit, ship-journey ×3, task-chat, and task-page ×2. At head it passes, 17/17.
- **Every removed guard keeps its null check** (`box ?`, `modelListEl ?`, `!drawer`, `!card`, `!root`/`!mount`, `activeEl &&`). `flight-companion.js:950` is equivalent on a real DOM. The walk starts at a click target under `modelListEl` and stops there, and `li &&` still ends the walk at a null `parentNode`.
- **Mutation checks.** I reverted each mutation afterwards.
  - Seeding `e.target.closest && …` into `session.js` fails the real-tree test.
  - Seeding a `typeof root.querySelectorAll !== 'function'` into `task-page.js` fails it.
  - Seeding a multi-line ternary into `ship-biscuit.js` fails it.
  - Deleting the LogicalExpression rule fails 3 tests, the Conditional rule 4, and the early-return rule 3.
  - Emptying the allow-list fails 1. Dropping `contains` from METHODS fails 2.
  - The tests go red for the reasons they name.
- **Residual grep** for every spelling, plus `?.(` and `'m' in`, across `public/`, `lib/`, `routes/` and `server.js`. The only matches are the three allow-listed `close-out.js` lines and `settings-models.js:61` (`phone.matches`, a MediaQueryList property, correctly not flagged).
- **Owning unit suites.** All 190 `tests/unit` files that name an edited file pass at head: 5,272 pass, 0 fail.
- **Regression.** `git log -S` on each removed guard shows each one came in with the feature that wrote it: LIN-3401, LIN-3371, LIN-3340, LIN-2068, and the LIN-4242→4293 refactor of `focusInCard`. None was a bug fix. No reverts touch these files. `focusInCard`'s callers pass a `querySelector` result or null.
- **Synthetic events.** No `public/` code dispatches click, input, change or focus events on `document`/`window`. The three `dispatchEvent` calls (`decision-panel.js:74/75/92`) target elements, so the delegated `e.target` removals hold.
- **Test level.** A source-shape AST check is the right level for a spelling rule. The behaviour stays unchanged, which the E2E and owning suites already show.

**Finding (inside):** the allow-list entry for `close-out.js:161` gives a reason the line no longer has. I deleted that one guard, leaving `main && main.getAttribute(...)`. `close-out-client.test.js` (18/18), `task-page-client`, `fake-dom-census` and the other owning suites stay green. Only the new test's stale-entry check fails. The PR body says so itself: "I did not verify that this one is strictly required; the suite's `<main>` stubs do have `getAttribute`." The ticket's scope call keeps `:159/161/175` for now, and LIN-4312 removes all three, so the line can stay. Its reason has to be true, though ("At merge: each entry has a true reason").

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (bounded class: allow-list entries with true present-tense reasons, "At merge" item 3). The `close-out.js: main && typeof main.getAttribute === 'function'` reason says the line is needed as a seam, but it is not. **Before the merge**, close-out changes that value in `tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js` `PRESENCE_ALLOW` to: `'kept by LIN-4304's scope call beside the :159/:175 seams, though not itself needed: close-out-client.test.js's <main> stubs define getAttribute (LIN-4312 removes it)'`. Then it runs `node --test tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js`, which should give 17/17. The key stays the same and there is no production change.
- **Inside** (bounded class: delegated `e.target` trusted on click/input/change/focusin/focusout/pointer events). A real browser never hands these listeners a non-Element target. **Discharged** before the merge by the synthetic-event grep above (no dispatch on `document`/`window` in `public/`), the event types each listener binds, and green E2E. **Named rollback:** revert the squash commit of #2320. It is client-only JS with no persisted data, so it is fully reversible.
- **Outside**, informational only: an optional call `x.m?.(…)` would be a fifth spelling the check does not see. There are zero instances today and the ticket bounded four spellings. A notebook note covers it, and no ticket is needed.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The work is complete against the plan and CI is green. The check is witnessed by mutation. The one fix is rewording the `close-out.js:161` allow-list reason, given above word for word.

## Close-out — LIN-4304

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2320, squash commit `f742e5ac` on main (pinned with `--match-head-commit 3b71bf96`). The Harbour / production deployment of `f742e5ac` reported `success`.

**What landed:** the 23 method-presence guards on `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `matches`, `closest`, `getAttribute` and `contains` are gone from `public/*.js` where the receiver is an Element by construction. Each keeps the null check it had. `tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js` is an acorn AST scan covering the four spellings, with fixtures and an allow-list. Three `close-out.js` `typeof` seams stay allow-listed until LIN-4312.

**Change I made after approval (review's one fix):**
- `3b71bf96` rewords the `PRESENCE_ALLOW` reason for `close-out.js: main && typeof main.getAttribute === 'function'`. This answers the review's inside finding that the old reason said the line was a needed seam when it is not. It uses the review's wording verbatim, the key is unchanged, and there is no production change.
- `node --test tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js` gives 17/17, both on the branch and on merged main.

**Ledger:**
- **Stale allow-list reason (inside):** fixed in `3b71bf96`, shown by the 17/17 run above.
- **Delegated `e.target` trusted (inside):** discharged before the merge by review's grep. Nothing in `public/` dispatches click, input, change or focus events on `document` or `window`, and the three `dispatchEvent` calls target elements. E2E is green. Named rollback, as review wrote it: revert the squash commit `f742e5ac`. The change is client-only JS with no persisted data.
- **Optional call `x.m?.(…)` as a fifth spelling (outside, informational):** zero instances today, and the ticket bounded four spellings. Review said a notebook note covers it and no ticket is needed, so I filed none.
- **Follow-ups filed:** none. The `typeof el.focus` guards, a shared scanner and the `readDispatch*` merge were named out of scope by the ticket itself. LIN-4312 already covers removing the `close-out.js` seams.

**CI:** green on the exact head `3b71bf96`, run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42107873415. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `CI success` all SUCCESS. The first head, `8cc40286`, was also green, with unit 23,828 pass / 0 fail and E2E 2,004 passed / 1 skipped (pre-existing).

**Post-deploy:** the ticket names no post-deploy steps. After the deploy landed I re-ran the check on merged main (17/17). I did not load the live pages in a browser. The E2E suite is the evidence for unchanged behaviour on a real DOM.

**Description:** snapshot captured and verified (the latest task snapshot matches the pre-prune description). The Implementation Plan section is pruned to a stub that keeps the `Implementation Plan` heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no`. Goal, Context, scope, acceptance and the Survey scope call are kept.

**Related tickets:** LIN-4312 (blocked by this) is unblocked and stays open. I left a note on it.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It wasn't, much: 19 one-line edits in 11 files. The change bound in two places. First, defining "a guard" precisely enough for an AST check: a method read that is tested and then called on the same receiver, where "governed" means the logical right side, the ternary branches, the `if` body, and the statements after an early-return `if`. Second, the hand-built test stubs, which could have made a removal throw. None did: every suite stayed green without touching a stub. Most of the cost was verification: baseline and after unit runs plus E2E, about 25 minutes for 21 changed lines.

**2. What first?** What I did: write the scanner and run it at base, so its hit list became the work list. With hindsight I'd also grep the stubs for which ones lack `closest`/`getAttribute`/`querySelectorAll`. That settles the seams up front.

**3. What I'd tidy.** (a) The allow-list key is the guard's text, so two identical guards in one file share one entry. A line-scoped key would be stricter. (b) The `close-out.js:161` entry: the suite's `<main>` stubs do have `getAttribute`, so its seam is weaker than the other two. Kept per the scope call; it probably goes. (c) The scanner is a fresh parse-and-walk inside one test file, next to fake-dom-census's. A shared AST helper would cut it to ~20 lines.

**4. If the area were how I'd want it,** this ticket wouldn't exist. LIN-4292 would have been "remove the idiom and add the check", drawn by idiom rather than by file, with the scan's output as its work list.

**5. What the ticket got wrong.** The hand count (~17 sites in ten files) undercounted: the scan found 23, including the `typeof` spelling. "An `e.target` can be a Text node" was wrong, and the Survey caught it. `flight-companion.js:950` was called legitimate but is removable, because the walk stops at `modelListEl`. The first wording asked for an inline marker, which the scope call replaced. A departure on my side: the plan said to run each file's owning suite after each file. I made all the edits and then ran the full suite once. It was green, but the step wasn't followed as written.

**6. Left behind.** New, with no obvious home: one more scanner. In two places: the close-out seams are now recorded in the allow-list and in `close-out.js`'s own comments, so LIN-4254 has to remove both. Not learned elsewhere: CLAUDE.md doesn't mention the check (by design); people meet it when it fails. Still there: the `typeof el.focus` guards, the same idiom on an unlisted method. Simpler: `public/` has one spelling, and `lib/`, `routes/` and `server.js` had no matches, so nothing waits there.

**7. Worth it as its own task?** The removals alone, no: 21 lines, carried by a Survey, two blind reads, a plan and a full verification cycle. They would have been cheaper inside LIN-4292, if it had been scoped by idiom. The check is the part with lasting value, and it fits a follow-on fine. What would have made this smaller: building the scanner first in LIN-4292, so its edges came from a list rather than from a reviewer's read. Later would cost about the same, but the idiom grows while nothing stops it.

relatedIssue.title: LIN-4254 piece 6: close-out-client onto loadWorld and remove close-out.js typeof seams (after LIN-4304)
